The oxime early labels were modest, and the naphthyl-alcohol transition labels were comparatively close to forecast, reducing the value of simply extending their previously high-error weak-eluent regions. The stronger-eluent nitrogen results were also more accurate in several cases, so follow-up targets missing loading relationships rather than a shared basic-nitrogen correction. All cited forecast errors are acquisition-time errors, not residuals of the current model.","batch_rationale":"The batch contains exactly 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs and has no pending experiments. It combines repair of demonstrated failures with experiments that discriminate between plausible local explanations and test structural transfer. The m120 panel addresses the largest new donor-response surprise, while m40's intermediate point connects its newly measured steep weak-eluent extension. The other carbonyl experiments test whether those corrections transfer to sterically substituted ketones, cyclic carbonyls, and an aldehyde whose onset and completion are decoupled. Loading experiments target separate endpoint associations in multifunctional esters and basic nitrogen compounds; the latest m194 result cautions against treating intermediate loading as a simple interpolation. The m168 pair changes only loading-solvent volume and tests a nearly absent model response to that feature. The m73 and m92 selections deliberately include one eligible replicate each, because stable unusual shapes and record variability imply different limits on prediction. The m209 follow-up is smaller after the latest bracketing observations localized its unusual record. The m72 pair measures a matched PE response while preserving the qualification that existing PE/DCM comparisons also change loading volume. Ratio-response pairs hold density, sample volume, loading solvent, and loading-solvent volume fixed. Singletons connect to measured anchors rather than opening unrelated grids. No two selections have identical molecule-plus-condition tuples, although two intentionally match previously observed tuples. These experiments may improve generalization across repeated structure-condition rows by teaching missing slopes, structural boundaries, injection sensitivity, and V1/V2 relationships. They do not optimize the selected separations or seek maximal retention. Cross-molecule comparisons remain conditional on the supplied loading conditions, and no absent concentration, flow, pH, or other column variables are assumed. Loading amount is the density-times-volume feature. Quantile spans and CW distances are supplementary evidence rather than acquisition rules; quantile spans are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width."}
